extracted.intended_audience: Department of Defense / Joint Force public affairs officers, PA planners, and JPASE/Defense Media Activity staff
extracted.subtask_description: Operational/public release and public affairs support guidance for Department of Defense joint public affairs practitioners, including OPSEC-related release constraints, DMA service offerings, JPASE capabilities and deployment/requests procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use general terms for units/equipment/supplies
rubrics_metrics.description: General terms should be used to describe units, equipment, and/or supplies available for support of combat units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid listing specific unit names, equipment models, or quantities that could reveal capabilities or logistics details.

rubrics_metrics.name: No disclosure of future plans/operations/strikes
rubrics_metrics.description: Any information that reveals details of future plans, operations, or strikes, including postponed or canceled operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not publicize planned or rescheduled operational activity; withhold any details that could enable adversary anticipation or preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not reveal specific locations or security posture
rubrics_metrics.description: Information and imagery that would reveal the specific location of military forces or show the level of security at military installations or encampments. For datelines, stories will state that the report originates from general regions unless a specific country has acknowledged its participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use regional datelines and avoid imagery or descriptive detail that permits geolocation or exposes force protection measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect rules of engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules of engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not disclose ROE to the public, since such information can compromise operations and force safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect intelligence activities and sources/methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Information on intelligence activities, including sources and methods, lists of targets, and battle damage assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclude any mention of intelligence collection techniques, source identities, target lists, or assessments that could reveal capabilities or compromise sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not disclose operational troop movement/size/deployments
rubrics_metrics.description: During an operation, specific information on friendly force troop movement or size, tactical deployments, and dispositions that would jeopardize OPSEC or lives. This would include unit designations and names of operations until released by the JFC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid publishing unit designators, force numbers, movements, or operation names until formally released by the Joint Force Commander.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not identify mission aircraft points of origin
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification of mission aircraft points of origin, other than as land- or carrier-based.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If mentioning aircraft, limit origin to broad categories (e.g., land- or carrier-based) rather than specific airfields or forward operating locations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not disclose weapon systems effectiveness or tactics
rubrics_metrics.description: Information on the effectiveness or ineffectiveness of weapon systems and tactics (to include, but not limited to adversary camouflage, cover, deception, targeting, direct and indirect fire, intelligence collection, or security measures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid assessments that reveal system performance, vulnerabilities, or tactical lessons that could be exploited by adversaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect identifying info during search and rescue
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific identifying information on missing or downed personnel, aircraft, or sunken ships while search and rescue operations are planned or underway.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withhold identifying details until SAR operations are complete or cleared for release, to protect personnel and operational security.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect special operations forces methods/equipment/tactics
rubrics_metrics.description: SOFs’ methods, equipment, or tactics which, if disclosed, would cause serious harm to the ability of these forces to accomplish their mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not release details of SOF procedures, gear, or tactics that could degrade their effectiveness or safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not reveal operational or support vulnerabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Information on operational or support vulnerabilities that could be used against US or allied units until that information no longer provides tactical advantage to the adversary and is, therefore, released by the JFC. Damage and casualties may be described as “light,” “moderate,” or “heavy.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If discussing damage/casualties, use only broad severity descriptors; withhold exploitable vulnerability details until JFC release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid specific operating methods and tactics
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific operating methods and tactics (e.g., offensive and defensive tactics or speed and formations). General terms such as “slow” or “fast” may be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only non-specific descriptors for operational tempo or methods to prevent disclosure of doctrine or maneuver patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on interviews/filming of EPWs/detainees
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for interviews or filming of EPWs or detained personnel must be coordinated through the staff judge advocate to ensure compliance with applicable laws and regulations including the law of war. Generally, photographing, filming, or other videotaping of EPWs or detained personnel for other than internal detention facility management purposes is likely to be prohibited. No individual in the custody or under the physical control of the USG, regardless of nationality or physical location, shall be subject to cruel, inhuman, or degrading treatment or punishment. Moreover, EPWs must at all times be protected against acts of violence or intimidation and against insults and public curiosity. Photos taken and used for nonofficial purposes may depict detainees in a degrading manner, thus violating international and US law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All requests involving detainees require legal coordination; default to prohibition except where expressly authorized for internal management or legally cleared purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact DMA for consolidated media capabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The DMA is a consolidation of several DOD and Service media capabilities. Joint force PA staff may contact the DMA through www.dma.mil to request the following capabilities:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use DMA as the central point for requesting cross-Service media assets and planning assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: AFRTS planning and support procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: DOD 5120.20-R, Management and Operation of American Forces Radio and Television Service, outlines basic procedures to obtain AFRTS service. Contact the DMA for additional guidance and planning assistance. The DMA can assist combatant command PA offices in planning and developing AFRTS systems to meet their contingency and CAP needs. Combatant command PA officials are responsible for planning for AFRTS in any operation as a joint command PA asset. The DMA encourage PA planners to involve the DMA in planning for exercise and during contingency operations. Extensive coordination may be required with other staff elements to coordinate communications frequency, power, and logistic requirements, based on the level of AFRTS support required for the operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage DMA early for AFRTS support; plan frequencies, power, and logistics; commanders must include AFRTS in PA planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: AFRTS deployable options and unit encouragement
rubrics_metrics.description: AFRTS has several flexible response options available to support any operational requirement. Deployable equipment systems range from a small satellite receiver that can be connected to a TV in a common viewing area with an approximate weight of 100 pounds, through a staffed radio station with an approximate weight of 550 pounds and four personnel, to a staffed radio and TV network designed to cover an entire operational area. It should be noted that the small satellite receiver systems are being obtained by individual units to be deployed as unit equipment. AFIS and/or AFRTS encourages individual units to obtain these systems. A listing of units with these receiver systems can be obtained from AFIS and/or AFRTS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider unit-level acquisition of small AFRTS satellite receiver kits for local morale/communications; coordinate larger AFRTS packages via DMA/AFIS.

rubrics_metrics.name: DIMOC imagery services and VI planning support
rubrics_metrics.description: The DMA’s DIMOC receives, processes, stores, and distributes classified and unclassified imagery products created by globally stationed and deployed DOD imagery producing personnel. The DIMOC also coordinates strategic VI requirements and plans with the DOD’s operational forces. This includes assisting planners with VI plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request imagery and VI planning assistance through DIMOC (specified URL); integrate DIMOC early into VI requirements and planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: DMA public-facing web operations support
rubrics_metrics.description: The DMA provides infrastructure for public-facing web pages for DOD customers. The DMA provides services necessary to create, sustain, maintain, and improve public-facing websites and their content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use DMA services for hosting and sustaining DOD public websites; coordinate content support and site planning with DMA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hometown News Program procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The DMA provides hometown news program support to the DOD and military departments. PA staffs submit DD Form 2266, Hometown News Release Information. DMA develops and provides the American public (through over 10,000 subscribing commercial media outlets) news releases about individual members of the Services including AC and RC members, academy/Reserve Officer Training Corps cadets, and civil servants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit DD Form 2266 for individual-service hometown releases; DMA handles distribution to subscribing commercial outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blogger engagement facilitation
rubrics_metrics.description: The DMA facilitates DOD-wide PA operations by linking citizen journalists (bloggers) with DOD leaders. This includes telephone conferencing and transcription services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use DMA to coordinate engagement with bloggers and citizen journalists and to manage conferencing/transcription logistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA and VI training via DINFOS
rubrics_metrics.description: The DMA’s DINFOS delivers PA, broadcasting, and VI training and education to initial, intermediate, and advanced-level DOD and interagency students (http://www.dinfos.dma.mil/).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan personnel training through DINFOS for PA, broadcasting, and visual information competencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emerging media assessment and transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: The DMA contributes to PA community proponency activities through the assessment, research, and testing of emerging media tools, techniques and technologies that may be of use within the DOD. This includes transfer of emerging media tools, techniques, and technologies to DOD components for practical application in PA operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate with DMA for trials and adoption of emerging media tools; DMA can provide research and testing support.

rubrics_metrics.name: JPASE provides expeditionary joint PA capability
rubrics_metrics.description: JPASE provides a trained, equipped, scalable, and expeditionary PA capability to include planning and media operations. JPASE is DOD’s only joint PA unit and deploys globally to support JTF commanders’ needs and provides scalable options that allow requesting combatant commands to tailor required capabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request JPASE when joint, expeditionary PA capabilities are needed and Organic/subordinate PA assets are insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: JPASE readiness/readiness colors and reserve integration
rubrics_metrics.description: The designation of global response force red, amber, or green relates to the degree of readiness of the team to deploy, with green being ready. This organization facilitates the integration of the JPASE reserves into operations and enhances command and control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider GRF color status when planning tasking and integration of JPASE reserve forces.

rubrics_metrics.name: JPASE deployment request & approval process
rubrics_metrics.description: JPASE deploys upon approval by the Commander, United States Joint Forces Command (CDRUSJFCOM). Commands request JPASE through approved force request processes in accordance with the USJFCOM joint enabling capability instructions. The CDRUSJFCOM has authority to approve JPASE deployments via a standing prepare to deploy order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initiate formal RFFs early; expect coordination and approvals through USJFCOM/J-3 channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request capabilities by scope, not by personnel count
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests must identify specific joint PA capabilities required by the scope and breadth of the operation not the number of people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When submitting requests, describe capabilities (e.g., media ops, VI support, accreditation) required rather than asking for X personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Involve JPASE early in operational planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Early involvement of JPASE personnel in mission planning will help JFCs develop an integrated communications strategy that enhances and guides initial planning and operations. JPASE personnel are readily available to participate in operational planning (via teleconference or in person) for emergent events prior to deployment approval and the movement of the JPASE team into the operational area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include JPASE in planning phases to optimize communications strategy and follow-on force employment.

rubrics_metrics.name: JPASE required support from requesting command
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications Systems: JPASE has very limited organic communications and information technology capability. Requesting commands must be prepared to provide, at a minimum, classified and unclassified connectivity, computers, and phones. Logistics: JPASE will require work spaces, billeting, messing, power, and transportation. Based on the need to move media from place to place, dedicated vehicular support may be required. Force Protection: JPASE personnel maintain ready inventory of personal protective equipment and are qualified with the 9mm pistol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure communications, logistics, and force protection support are planned and provided by the requesting command before JPASE deployment.

rubrics_metrics.name: JPASE size, availability, and duration expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: The capacity of JPASE to support deployments will vary based on personnel available and other operational requirements. JPASE typically maintains a ready team of eight personnel capable of responding to missions for a duration of 90-120 days. If JPASE can support a deployment request, team members should be available on site 72 hours after notification (N+48).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for typical JPASE team size (~8) and 90–120 day support windows; expect a rapid response timeline (target on-site within ~72 hours) though exact N+ timing is situational.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record and submit change recommendations and comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Users in the field are highly encouraged to submit comments on this publication ... These comments should address content (accuracy, usefulness, consistency, and organization), writing, and appearance. Recommendations for urgent changes to this publication should be submitted to specified CDRUSJFCOM addresses; routine changes should be submitted electronically via the CJCS Joint Electronic Library. When a Joint Staff directorate submits a proposal to the CJCS that would change source document information reflected in this publication, that directorate will include a proposed change to this publication as an enclosure to its proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the stated routing for urgent vs. routine changes; include proposed text when source documents change; maintain the Record of Changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution and reproduction restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Local reproduction is authorized and access to unclassified publications is unrestricted. However, access to and reproduction authorization for classified joint publications must be in accordance with DOD 5200.1-R, Information Security Program. The Joint Staff J-7 will not print copies of JPs for distribution. Electronic versions are available on JDEIS (NIPRNET/SIPRNET) and on the JEL. Only approved joint publications and joint test publications are releasable outside the combatant commands, Services, and Joint Staff. Release of any classified joint publication to foreign governments or foreign nationals must be requested through the local embassy (Defense Attaché Office) to DIA, Defense Foreign Liaison/IE-3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distribute unclassified JP content locally as needed; follow DOD security directives for classified materials; route foreign-release requests via diplomatic channels to DIA.
